Add a README badge of the engine release

Source: R/use-vanilla.R
use_vanilla_badge.Rd

Writes the file .github/inlavanilla-badge.json in the package whose root is path, and prints the line to add to its README. The badge reads "vanilla", with the release of inlavanilla that the lock inst/inlavanilla.lock names, such as "v26.11.25-2", in vanilla colours.

The badge is not a fixed image. The README line asks shields.io to draw it from the file on GitHub, so it shows the release of the copy on the branch branch as soon as that file is pushed. use_vanilla() rewrites the file whenever it updates the copy, so the badge follows the lock. Commit the file with the lock.

It also adds ^\.github$ to .Rbuildignore where that line is missing, so that R CMD build leaves the folder out.

It is optional: use_vanilla() does not add it, and offers it at the end of its list.

Usage

use_vanilla_badge(path = ".", branch = "main")

Arguments

path

The root of the package, or a folder inside it. By default the working directory.

branch

The branch of the package on GitHub whose file the badge reads. By default "main".

Value

Invisibly, the README line, as Markdown. It takes the GitHub repository of the package from the URL or BugReports field of its DESCRIPTION. Where neither names one, the line holds OWNER/REPO, to be replaced by hand.

See also

use_vanilla(), which keeps the badge in step with the lock.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# From the root of a package that holds a copy of the engine
use_vanilla_badge()
} # }
